Inbound via self-serve signups; spinning up hosted API keys in staging.

Overview: HoneyBranch builds lightweight AI-driven product discovery widgets (search + recommendations) and an order-assist chat for SMB storefronts. They're small, engineering-led, scaling to 200 merchants. Main blocker is inference cost when enabling chat+embeddings for every merchant. They want a pragmatic cost plan before scaling.

Traffic & usage signals called out: 
- Baseline tokens: ~2.5M tokens/month (staging+some prod).
- Peak events (campaigns/holiday): single-day spikes to ~7M tokens.
- Prompt anatomy: average user prompt ~60 tokens; contextual metadata adds ~240 tokens (user history + product snippets).
- Typical generation: 40-120 tokens per response; embeddings run on product catalog shards (batch size currently 1 per item, expensive).
- Latency requirement: p95 <300ms for chat on small catalogs; will tolerate up to 700ms on heavy reranks.
- Goal: reduce per-token spend by ~35-45% to justify rolling out to more merchants.

Explicit asks on discovery call: 
- Can Hosted API adopt batching on embeddings ingestion (they currently do item-by-item).
- Prefix/KV caching for cart and repeat-user flows to avoid re-sending full context.
- Prompt templating / compression examples to cut redundant metadata.
- Quick token-usage audit + prioritized list of low-friction wins.
- Sample $ projection showing savings with batching (2x), caching (prefix), and simple prompt compression.

Security / infra notes: 
- Tech stack: Node.js backend, Firebase auth, Postgres metadata, AWS (us-west-2).
- Prefer Redwood-hosted (no infra changes) but may explore Dedicated if residency or specialized SLAs needed later.
- Compliance: SOC2 is required for payment partners; SSO for admin access planned.
